parsed.explanation: This is a thin dossier: no source addresses border screening, document/marker rules, gendered facilities, custody, healthcare or violence for trans visitors. What exists is structural and positive — a rule-of-law framework with strict general anti-discrimination law applied uniformly, a registry that has performed a visitors' same-sex union since 2012, and a tourism sector actively courting LGBTQ visitors. No trans-specific criminalisation, police targeting, facility exclusion or hostility is documented anywhere. But marriage equality and general anti-discrimination law are climate signals, not traveller protections, and the statute is not shown to name gender identity or to have been enforced on those grounds. Extrapolating from a functioning, accepting institutional climate with no known traveller-facing exposure, offset by fully open questions on documents, facilities and remedies, I place this in the lower half of Reduced Risk — a step below the tier with documented, operating trans-specific protections. Silence here is moderately favourable (institutions that function leave records), but it is not proof of safety.
